_comment: Action registry. Each entry references an NPC key from _maps/npcs/registry.json and lists their actions. Use _action_templates as reference for authoring new actions.
Taterzens paths are set exclusively in-game via the path editor.
Enter editor: /npc edit path  |  Exit editor: /npc edit path  |  Clear: /npc edit path clear
In the editor, left-click a block to add it as a node (turns red); right-click to remove.
The 'waypoints' array below is a planning reference — use these coordinates to know where to click in-game.
Fallback (single destination, no loop): /npc action goto <x> <y> <z>
Sets the NPC's movement behaviour.
Types: NONE | FORCED_LOOK | FORCED_PATH | PATH | FOLLOW | FREE
FORCED_LOOK: looks at players within 4 blocks.
PATH: follows path with rests and look-arounds.
FORCED_PATH: follows path strictly, no rests.
FOLLOW: pursues a target. Requires 'target' field (name or UUID).
FREE: wanders freely inside an enclosed area.
NONE: stationary.
Runs a give command when a player right-clicks the NPC.
--clicker-- is replaced at runtime with the interacting player's name.
Permission level must be >= 2 for the give command to execute.
Set permission level: /npc edit commands setPermissionLevel 2
Starts a Blabber dialog when a player right-clicks the NPC.
target: '--clicker--' for the interacting player, or any selector for someone else.
interlocutor: selector for the NPC entity itself (optional but recommended for @interlocutor use in dialog).
Dialog file must exist at: data/luminacion/blabber/dialogues/<dialog_name>.json
Permission level must be >= 2.
Set permission level: /npc edit commands setPermissionLevel 2
blabber_dialog._command: /npc edit commands add minecraft blabber dialogue start luminacion:<dialog_name> --clicker-- @e[type=<type>,limit=1,sort=nearest]

_comment: Convention for pausing any NPC's routine while it's talking to a player, and
resuming it afterwards. Applies to EVERY NPC, regardless of movement mode —
including NONE. This used to be scoped to 'any NPC whose movement mode isn't
NONE', which was wrong: confirmed on Khaoe (2026-07-25, the pack's first NONE
npc actually built) that her skin never healed after a failed mineskin fetch,
because she shipped without check_proximity/heal_skin at all under the old
rule. The async skin-fetch race (see 'Why heal_skin.mcfunction exists' below)
and the mid-dialog pause/resume tagging both apply to a stationary NPC exactly
as much as a roaming one — movement mode was never actually the right gate.
For a NONE npc, resume_routine.mcfunction's movement line is just 'npc edit
movement NONE' again (a no-op on behavior), but the tag cleanup and the
periodic heal_skin/heal_path calls it unlocks still matter.
Files involved:
functions/npcs/_shared/pause_routine.mcfunction   — shared, sets movement FORCED_LOOK + tags 'luminacion.paused'
functions/npcs/_shared/enter_dialog.mcfunction    — shared, calls pause_routine + tags 'luminacion.in_dialog'
_templates/npcs/resume_routine.mcfunction   — per NPC, restores this NPC's movement mode
_templates/npcs/check_proximity.mcfunction  — per NPC, tick-based stop/resume within 2 blocks
_templates/npcs/heal_skin.mcfunction        — per NPC, tick-based skin self-heal (see below)
_templates/npcs/heal_path.mcfunction        — per NPC, tick-based path self-heal (see 'scripted_path' below)
_templates/npcs/end_with_gift.mcfunction    — per NPC, pattern for endings combining give+resume
data/luminacion/tags/functions/npc_routine_tick.json — registry: add each NPC's check_proximity.mcfunction here
Setup for a given NPC:
1. Right-click actions (spawn.mcfunction) start with:
npc edit commands add minecraft function luminacion:npcs/_shared/enter_dialog
before 'blabber dialogue start ...'.
2. Every end_dialogue state in that NPC's dialogs calls (directly, or via a
combined-effect function like end_with_gift.mcfunction):
execute as @interlocutor run function luminacion:npcs/<npc_key>/resume_routine
3. Duplicate resume_routine.mcfunction, check_proximity.mcfunction,
heal_skin.mcfunction and heal_path.mcfunction into functions/npcs/<npc_key>/,
and register check_proximity.mcfunction in npc_routine_tick.json (the two
heal_*.mcfunction files are called from check_proximity.mcfunction directly,
no separate registration).
Why heal_skin.mcfunction exists: Taterzens fetches skins asynchronously from
mineskin.org on a background thread, decoupled from anything else touching the
NPC (e.g. deselecting it before the fetch lands). That race can leave the skin
permanently unset. check_proximity.mcfunction calls heal_skin.mcfunction every
100 ticks, which re-requests the skin only if TaterzenNPCTag.skin.value is
currently missing — a no-op once it's actually set.
Why both an end_dialogue action AND a tick-based check: Blabber does not run
end_dialogue actions if the player exits the dialog early (Escape / disconnect),
so the tick check (stop within 2 blocks, resume once no player is within a wider
radius) is the safety net that guarantees the NPC never gets stuck paused.
IMPORTANT — the resume check's radius must NOT be the same 2 blocks used for the initial
pause trigger, and must NOT be narrower than the game's actual interact/reach range.
Originally was 2 blocks on both lines, reasoned (wrongly) to be safe without checking
luminacion.in_dialog because 'Blabber's dialogue screen freezes player movement while open,
so distance can only exceed 2 blocks after the dialog has actually closed.' That reasoning
only holds if the player was ALREADY within 2 blocks at the moment they clicked — but
Taterzens has no interact-range override (confirmed: config/Taterzens/config.json has no
such setting, so it's plain vanilla entity reach — 3 blocks survival, 6 blocks creative as of
the 1.20 reach-attribute split). A click from beyond 2 blocks (trivial in creative, and not
even unusual in survival) opens the dialog while frozen at a distance the resume check
already reads as 'nobody nearby' — so it undoes the pause on literally the very next tick,
while the dialogue is still open. Confirmed in-game on Döran, 2026-07-25: this is what caused
him to visibly wander off mid-conversation (movement flipped back to his roaming mode) and,
as a side effect, swallowed his nod animations (the walk/path logic overwrites head rotation
every tick, fighting the nod's own relative-rotation writes).
Fix: keep the PAUSE trigger ('if entity @a[distance=..2] run pause_routine') at 2 blocks —
that one only controls how early an approaching player gets noticed, no reach concern there.
Widen the RESUME safety-net's threshold to 'unless entity @a[distance=..6]' — comfortably
past creative reach, so a dialog opened from any legal click distance stays paused for its
entire (frozen) duration, and the safety net still fires once the player genuinely leaves
after actually closing the dialog. This is a template-level fix — check_proximity.mcfunction
for every NPC needs the wider resume radius, not just the one being currently debugged.
Confirmed from Blabber's PlayerDialogueTracker source that the screen-freeze premise itself
is accurate; the bug was purely the radius mismatch, not the underlying reasoning about
freezing.
Convention for giving a PATH/FORCED_PATH NPC its waypoints. Do NOT use Taterzens'
in-game '/npc edit path' left-click editor — a stray click silently adds/removes
nodes, and clearing nodes afterward (even deliberately, via '/npc edit path clear')
does not clear Taterzens' internal movement restriction, so the NPC keeps walking
toward the last point it was restricted to even with an empty path. Confirmed via
Taterzens 1.11.7+1.20.1 source: DirectPathGoal/LazyPathGoal navigate using
getRestrictCenter(), independent of the PathTargets list, and clearPathTargets()
never resets it.
Instead, each path is its own function that sets PathTargets directly via
'/data merge entity', which was confirmed in-game to retroactively trigger
Taterzens' own NBT-load logic (including its restrictTo() call) on a live entity,
exactly as if it had just been freshly loaded — so the restriction ends up correct
with no editor involved.
Files involved:
_templates/npcs/paths/select_path.mcfunction — per path, sets one named route active
_templates/npcs/heal_path.mcfunction          — per NPC, tick-based path self-heal
Setup for a given NPC with a roaming route:
1. Duplicate select_path.mcfunction as functions/npcs/<npc_key>/paths/<path_name>.mcfunction
for each named route this NPC has, filling in its waypoints.
2. Run one of them as an operator to activate it: teleports the NPC to the first
waypoint (so switching paths is always clean, regardless of where the NPC
currently is), sets PathTargets, sets movement PATH, and records the active
path's name in the 'luminacion:npcs' command storage.
3. Add a matching line to functions/npcs/<npc_key>/heal_path.mcfunction for each
path defined, so it self-heals if PathTargets ever goes empty.
Multiple named paths per NPC are supported this way — switching between them is
just running a different paths/<name>.mcfunction. Only one can be active at a time
(tracked by the 'active_path' storage value), and heal_path.mcfunction only
restores whichever one is currently marked active.
Convention for an NPC that switches between multiple named 'states' at runtime —
e.g. standing still for one scene vs. roaming with a different dialog wired up.
Only needed when an NPC genuinely has more than one movement mode over its
lifetime; a single-mode NPC just uses routine_pause_resume/scripted_path directly,
no states/ folder needed.
Files involved:
_templates/npcs/states/stationary_state.mcfunction — a NONE state: no teleport,
no enter_dialog/pause_routine wiring (nothing to pause)
_templates/npcs/states/roaming_state.mcfunction    — a PATH state: teleport to
waypoint 0 + PathTargets (same mechanism as scripted_path), DOES wire
enter_dialog/pause_routine (there's a real routine to pause here)
Setup for a given NPC with multiple states:
1. Duplicate one of the two templates above per state into
functions/npcs/<npc_key>/states/<state_name>.mcfunction.
2. spawn.mcfunction should NOT set movement or right-click commands directly —
end it by calling one state function instead (whichever is the NPC's default),
e.g. 'function luminacion:npcs/<npc_key>/states/<default_state_name>'.
3. check_proximity.mcfunction (and heal_path.mcfunction's checks) must be gated
on 'active_state' being this NPC's roaming state name — see the worked example
below. Without this gating, resume_routine.mcfunction (hardcoded to a single
movement mode) would force the NPC back into its roaming state after ANY
dialog ends, even one that happened during a deliberately stationary state.
4. Any dialog wired from a stationary state must NOT call resume_routine on its
end_dialogue action — nothing to resume. Any dialog wired from a roaming
state SHOULD call it, same as a single-state roaming NPC.
Worked example (check_proximity.mcfunction gating, <npc_key> has states
'hangar' (NONE) and 'roaming' (PATH)):

execute if data storage luminacion:npcs {<npc_key>:{active_state:"roaming"}} as @e[type=taterzens:npc,name=<display_name>,limit=1,tag=!luminacion.paused] at @s if entity @a[distance=..2] run function luminacion:npcs/_shared/pause_routine

execute if data storage luminacion:npcs {<npc_key>:{active_state:"roaming"}} as @e[type=taterzens:npc,name=<display_name>,limit=1,tag=luminacion.paused] at @s unless entity @a[distance=..2] run function luminacion:npcs/<npc_key>/resume_routine
execute if data storage luminacion:npcs {<npc_key>:{active_state:"roaming"}} if score <npc_key>_heal_cd luminacion.int matches 100.. run function luminacion:npcs/<npc_key>/heal_path
heal_skin.mcfunction is NOT gated — skin correctness doesn't depend on movement
mode, so it stays on the same 100-tick cooldown regardless of active_state.
First worked example: nuvilo and nerkeli (Feria del Milenio hangar scene vs. solo
roaming dialogs).
Convention for a dialog that starts when a player walks within range of an NPC, instead of
right-clicking it. First worked example: nuvilo_nerkeli_feria_del_milenio (2026-07-26, the
hangar scene from multi_state_npc above) — the eavesdrop scene now starts the moment a player
gets within 2 blocks of EITHER Nuvilo or Nerkeli, rather than requiring a click on Nuvilo.
Files involved (this worked example):
functions/npcs/nuvilo/hangar_dialog_tick.mcfunction  — the trigger + guard logic
functions/npcs/nuvilo/start_hangar_dialog.mcfunction — actually starts the dialog
data/luminacion/tags/functions/npc_routine_tick.json — hangar_dialog_tick registered here
Right-click wiring is removed entirely for a proximity-triggered dialog — states/hangar.mcfunction
runs 'npc edit commands clear' and adds nothing back for this scene.
GATING (multi-NPC scene, e.g. two NPCs meant to be standing together): don't trust the two
NPCs' active_state flags alone as proof they're actually near each other — states/hangar.mcfunction
never teleports either one (positioned manually), so a misplaced NPC could otherwise still fire
the scene alone. Add an explicit distance check between the two NPCs themselves on top of the
state check. This worked example uses 3 blocks for that NPC-to-NPC check (tighter than the
player-facing radii below — tuned down from an initial 6 per user request, 2026-07-26).
TARGETING: since there's no right-click, there's no --clicker--. Use an explicit selector
instead, e.g. '@a[distance=..2,sort=nearest,limit=1]' switched into via 'execute as ... at @s
run blabber dialogue start <dialog_id> @s <interlocutor_selector>' — safe to call from inside a
regular .mcfunction (unlike --clicker--, which only substitutes correctly in a top-level command
added via 'npc edit commands add' — see random_dialog below for that caveat's original writeup).
GUARD: use a value in the 'luminacion:npcs' command storage (the same storage active_state
already lives in), NOT an entity tag, whenever more than one NPC's proximity can fire the same
trigger — a tag only lives on whichever entity set it, so a check from the OTHER NPC wouldn't
see it. A storage flag is readable from either NPC's execution context. Prevents re-triggering
every tick while a player stays inside the radius for the whole (frozen) dialog. Clear it using
the same asymmetric enter/exit radius the pause/resume dance uses elsewhere (2 in, 6 out for the
player-facing check) — checked against BOTH NPCs in a multi-NPC scene, since either one's
proximity could have opened the dialog, so both must be clear of nearby players before the
guard resets and a later approach can replay the scene.
Convention for an NPC with multiple independent dialogs that should be picked at random on
right-click, rather than always firing the same one. First worked example: Döran (three
Plaza de las Culturas dialogs — doran_plaza_orientation, doran_four_castles,
doran_eras_of_culture — equal odds).
Right-click actions are a flat list of commands that ALL fire on every click (see
blabber_dialog above) — there's no branching construct in Taterzens' own command list, so a
roll-then-dispatch has to be built from vanilla commands added as separate top-level entries:
1. A per-NPC helper function does the roll — NOT added directly as an 'execute ... run
random value ...' command:
npc edit commands add minecraft function luminacion:npcs/<npc_key>/roll_dialog
2. One command per dialog option, each gated on a different roll result, added directly
(this DOES work added this way, unlike the roll — see below):

npc edit commands add minecraft execute if score <npc_key>_dialog_roll luminacion.int matches <i> run blabber dialogue start luminacion:<dialog_id> --clicker-- @e[name=<display_name>,limit=1,sort=nearest]
DOES NOT use the vanilla /random command — confirmed in-game (Döran, 2026-07-25) that /random
is unavailable in this pack's actual server environment, full stop. First suspected this was
specific to nesting inside Taterzens' 'npc edit commands add' argument (the failure — a
Brigadier parse error landing exactly at the start of 'random', with 'execute ... run' parsing
fine up through 'run' — looked like a Taterzens grammar restriction). Ruled that out by moving
the identical line into a plain top-level .mcfunction line instead (no Taterzens argument
involved at all): same exact failure, same exact position. Nothing else in this heavily-modded
pack's logs successfully invokes /random either. Root cause undetermined (some mod removing or
shadowing the command, most likely) — not worth chasing further when a command-free
alternative covers the actual need. roll_dialog.mcfunction instead reads elapsed world time and
reduces it mod N via a scoreboard operation:
execute store result score <npc_key>_dialog_roll luminacion.int run time query gametime
scoreboard players set <npc_key>_roll_mod luminacion.int <N>
scoreboard players operation <npc_key>_dialog_roll luminacion.int %= <npc_key>_roll_mod luminacion.int
scoreboard players add <npc_key>_dialog_roll luminacion.int 1
(the last line shifts the 0..N-1 modulo result to 1..N to match the 'matches <i>' gates
above). Not cryptographically random — a player could in principle time a click to land
on a chosen tick — but that bar was never the point; this only needs to vary which of a
few greeting lines shows. '<npc_key>_roll_mod' is a disposable scratch constant, reset
every call, never read anywhere else.
IMPORTANT — quote <display_name> in EVERY vanilla @e[...] selector referencing it
(@e[name="<display_name>",...]) if it contains anything outside Brigadier's
unquoted-string charset (letters, digits, '_', '-', '.', '+') — an umlaut/diaeresis (Döran,
Dägna) included. Confirmed in-game: an unquoted 'ö' breaks the selector parse mid-token
('Expected end of options'), a separate failure mode from the /random one above but hit the
same day building Döran. Applies to every @e[...] selector referencing such a name — not
just this pattern — so also fix it in check_proximity.mcfunction and heal_skin.mcfunction.
Do NOT extend this quoting fix to 'npc create <name>' itself — confirmed in-game that this
is the OPPOSITE mistake and breaks a working NPC. 'npc create <name>' is Taterzens' own
argument, not a vanilla entity selector, and it does not strip surrounding quote characters —
quoting it ('npc create "Döran"') creates an NPC whose actual name literally includes the
quote marks, which then mismatches every @e[name="<display_name>",...] selector elsewhere
(they're looking for the name without quotes). This argument accepts raw non-ASCII characters
unquoted with no complaint — 'npc create Döran', unquoted, is correct and was never the
source of any parse error; only the selectors ever needed quoting.
For unequal weighting, gate more than one 'matches <i>' value on the same dialog (e.g. roll
1..4, matches 1..2 for the favored dialog, matches 3/4 for the other two).
Why the DISPATCH commands (step 2) stay directly-added rather than also going through a
wrapper function: --clicker-- is a Taterzens placeholder substituted into the literal text of
a command at the moment it's added via 'npc edit commands add' — every existing NPC only ever
uses it inside a directly-added top-level command line (confirmed by grep: no precedent of
--clicker-- inside a called .mcfunction anywhere in this pack). Moving a blabber dialogue
start line inside a nested function would leave --clicker-- unsubstituted there, breaking the
dialog target. The roll (step 1) has no such constraint — it never contains --clicker--, so
it's free to live in its own function regardless of the /random finding above.
If this NPC's movement mode isn't NONE, enter_dialog is still the very first added command
(before the roll), same as any single-dialog roaming NPC — see routine_pause_resume above.
Each dialog's own end_dialogue action calls resume_routine as normal; randomization only
picks which dialog starts, not how any of them end.
Register all N dialogs under this NPC's key in _maps/dialogs/registry.json as normal —
nothing about the registry format changes, this is purely a spawn.mcfunction wiring pattern.
Reads or writes a variable using scoreboard objectives.
Two objectives are used as data types:
luminacion.bool  — dummy objective, values: 0 (false) or 1 (true)
luminacion.int   — dummy objective, any integer value
The score holder name IS the variable name (fake player convention).
Operations: set | add | subtract | reset | test (compare)
Example: scoreboard players set quest_started luminacion.bool 1
These objectives must be initialised once via load function:
scoreboard objectives add luminacion.bool dummy
scoreboard objectives add luminacion.int dummy
